sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Match the surfaces (Column I) with maintenance (Column II). I: (1) Polished wood (2) Cane (3) Plastics (4) Iron. II: (a) Smear oil and use brick powder (b) Methylated spirit, turpentine or mild ammonia (c) Coat with clear varnish (d) Apply kerosene and keep in the sun.

There are turmeric stains on your marble floor. Part A: What should be the first step to clean the marble floor? (a) Rub with lemon juice (b) Use hot water and detergent (c) Apply kerosene oil (d) Wipe corners and sides daily. Part B: What should be done after cleaning to maintain the marble's whiteness?
questions.answer: Part A: (b) use hot water and detergent. Part B: rub with lemon juice.

questions.q: Suggest the exact cause. (a) The fuse has blown. (b) The fan is noisy. (c) The tap is leaking.
questions.answer: (a) The wire in the cut-out melted on heavy current. (b) Worn-out bearings. (c) The washer needs to be replaced.

questions.q: True or False. (a) Acid should be rinsed immediately from ceramic tiles. (b) Carpets should be rolled up while damp.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: they should be dried thoroughly before rolling.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps to clean a coir floor covering (two points) and one precaution.
questions.answer: Clean it daily with a coarse broom and shake it out occasionally. If very dirty, wash in soapy water, rinse in cold salty water and dry completely in the open air; do not let it get very dirty.

questions.q: Suggest four ways to prevent electric shock at home.
questions.answer: Keep hands dry and wear rubber slippers when handling appliances. Switch off and unplug before repairs, replace worn wires and use ISI marked appliances.

questions.q: How will you clean a stained wooden chopping board?
questions.answer: Wash it with mild soap and warm water, scrubbing along the grain. Remove stuck food with the back of a knife and dry it in the open air.

questions.q: Why should a non-stick pan be rinsed immediately after use and cleaned with a sponge?
questions.answer: Hard scrubbers and steel wool scratch the Teflon coating. Rinsing at once and a sponge with soapy water keep it intact.

questions.q: What is the first thing to check when an electrical appliance stops working?
questions.answer: The electric supply to it, and the plug and fuse. Always disconnect it from the main supply before any repair.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps to clean a coir floor covering, including maintenance and precautions.
questions.answer: (i) Clean it daily with a coarse broom or brush and occasionally turn it upside down and shake out the dust. (ii) If very dirty, wash with soapy water and rinse in cold salty water. (iii) Dry it completely in open air and do not let it get very dirty.

questions.q: Explain the steps to clean a glass surface properly, including maintenance and precautions.
questions.answer: (i) Clean with a wad of newspaper and water; add vinegar to the rinse water for shine. (ii) Remove grease stains with ammonia in warm water and fly specks with methylated spirit. (iii) Do not use hard scrubbers or abrasives as they scratch.

questions.q: Explain how to change the washer of a leaking tap (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Turn off the mains and unscrew the hand-wheel. (ii) Remove the headgear using two wrenches and take out the stem with the washer. (iii) Replace the old washer with a new one and fix everything back.

questions.q: Explain how to maintain a carpet (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Clean regularly; once a month shake it or vacuum it. (ii) Wash a colour-fast carpet with a soap lather, rinse and dry in the sun. (iii) Put naphthalene balls in rolled carpets, air them and remove stains at once.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Give suggestions for maintaining at home: carpets, wooden surfaces, brass, glass windows, cane chair and coir flooring.
questions.answer: (i) Carpets: shake monthly, vacuum, wash colour-fast ones with lather and dry in the sun. (ii) Wood: wipe with mild soap, dry, rub polished wood with flannel and remove water marks with spirit or ammonia. (iii) Brass: lemon with salt, tamarind or ash with fine steel wool; engraved brass with an old toothbrush. (iv) Glass: newspaper and vinegar water. (v) Cane: warm salty water, dry in the open and varnish. (vi) Coir: sweep daily, wash with soapy water, rinse in salty water and dry.
